# meshstack_workspace_user_group_member (Resource)

One member of a workspace user group. Use it to add a user to a group whose other members are managed elsewhere, for example in meshPanel or in another Terraform configuration.

~> **Do not combine with `spec.members`.** If `meshstack_workspace_user_group` sets `spec.members` for the same group, each apply of one resource removes the members the other adds.

~> **The whole group is written on every change.** The meshObject API has no endpoint for a single member, so each create and delete reads the group and writes it back with the member added or removed. The provider applies the changes to one group one after another within an apply, but a change to the group by anything else between that read and write is lost.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "meshstack_workspace_user_group_member" "example" {
  group_ref = meshstack_workspace_user_group.example.ref
  user_ref  = data.meshstack_user.example.ref
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_ref` (Attributes) Reference to the workspace user group, such as `meshstack_workspace_user_group.example.ref`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_ref))
- `user_ref` (Attributes) Reference to the user who becomes a member, such as `data.meshstack_user.example.ref`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user_ref))

<a id="nestedatt--group_ref"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group_ref`

Required:

- `name` (String) Named identifier (`metadata.name`) of the `meshWorkspaceUserGroup`.
- `owned_by_workspace` (String) Named identifier (`metadata.name`) of the `meshWorkspace` that owns the `meshWorkspaceUserGroup`.

Optional:

- `kind` (String) meshObject type, always `meshWorkspaceUserGroup`.


<a id="nestedatt--user_ref"></a>
### Nested Schema for `user_ref`

Required:

- `name` (String) Named identifier (`metadata.name`) of `meshUser`.

Optional:

- `kind` (String) meshObject type, always `meshUser`.

## Import

Use the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with an appropriate `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  # <workspace-identifier>.<group-identifier>.<username>
  id = "my-workspace.my-user-group.jane.doe@example.com"
  to = meshstack_workspace_user_group_member.example
}
```

To generate the full resource configuration from the existing remote state, add the `import` block above to your configuration and then run:

```shell
tofu plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
# Terraform equivalent:
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated_resources.tf
```

Copy the generated configuration into your root module to start managing the resource with OpenTofu or Terraform.
Note that the generated configuration may require minor adjustments or cleanup, so always run `tofu plan` / `terraform plan` afterwards to verify 
that the configuration fully matches the imported state and that no unintended changes are pending.
If the plan only shows the import of the resource (no other changes), you can run `tofu apply` / `terraform apply` to complete the import. From that point on,
the resource is fully managed via OpenTofu or Terraform.
